documents.title: Office Visit Note
documents.text:
PROGRESS NOTE
Reason for Visit: Follow-up for diabetes.
Subjective: 57-year-old man. Here for routine diabetes follow-up. Reports inconsistent metformin use and increased thirst.
Objective: Foot exam normal. Monofilament sensation intact. Retinal exam due.
Assessment:
1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus with hyperglycemia
2. Obesity
3. Hyperlipidemia
Plan: Increase metformin to 1000 mg BID, start atorvastatin 40 mg nightly, refer to diabetes education, repeat A1c in 3 months.

documents.title: Discharge Summary
documents.text:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Chief Complaint: Worsening shortness of breath.
History of Present Illness: 75-year-old man presenting with worsening shortness of breath. Increased dyspnea, wheeze and sputum production for 3 days. 40 pack-year smoking history.
Hospital Course: Treated with nebulized bronchodilators, prednisone 40 mg and doxycycline. Ambulatory saturation 91% on room air at discharge.
Discharge Diagnoses:
1. COPD with acute exacerbation
2. Tobacco use disorder
Discharge Plan: Prednisone taper, tiotropium daily, smoking cessation counseling, pulmonology follow-up.

documents.title: XR Chest 2 Views
documents.text:
XR CHEST 2 VIEWS
Clinical Indication: Worsening shortness of breath.
Technique: Standard protocol.
Findings: Hyperinflated lungs with flattened hemidiaphragms. No focal consolidation or effusion.
Impression: Hyperinflation consistent with COPD. No acute process.

encounter.reason: Nephrology follow-up for chronic kidney disease

documents.title: Office Visit Note
documents.text:
PROGRESS NOTE
Reason for Visit: Nephrology follow-up for chronic kidney disease.
Subjective: 84-year-old woman. Known CKD secondary to hypertensive nephrosclerosis. Reports mild fatigue. No edema.
Objective: Creatinine above prior baseline of 1.8. Potassium elevated.
Assessment:
1. Chronic kidney disease stage 3b
2. Anemia of chronic kidney disease
Plan: Low-potassium diet, hold lisinopril pending repeat BMP in 1 week, start ESA evaluation.

documents.title: US Renal Bilateral
documents.text:
US RENAL BILATERAL
Clinical Indication: Nephrology follow-up for chronic kidney disease.
Technique: Standard protocol.
Findings: Right kidney 9.1 cm, left kidney 9.4 cm. Increased cortical echogenicity bilaterally. No hydronephrosis.
Impression: Bilateral echogenic kidneys consistent with medical renal disease. No hydronephrosis.

documents.title: Office Visit Note
documents.text:
PROGRESS NOTE
Reason for Visit: Fatigue and weight gain.
Subjective: 42-year-old man. Six months of fatigue, cold intolerance, constipation and 5 kg weight gain.
Objective: Thyroid not enlarged on exam. Delayed relaxation of reflexes.
Assessment:
1. Primary hypothyroidism
Plan: Start levothyroxine 50 mcg daily, repeat TSH in 6 weeks.

documents.title: Discharge Summary
documents.text:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Chief Complaint: Right lower quadrant abdominal pain.
History of Present Illness: 30-year-old man presenting with right lower quadrant abdominal pain. Periumbilical pain migrating to the right lower quadrant over 18 hours with anorexia and nausea.
Hospital Course: Underwent uncomplicated laparoscopic appendectomy. Tolerated diet on postoperative day 1.
Discharge Diagnoses:
1. Acute appendicitis, status post laparoscopic appendectomy
Discharge Plan: No lifting over 10 lb for 2 weeks. Surgical clinic follow-up in 10 days.

documents.title: CT Abdomen and Pelvis with Contrast
documents.text:
CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITH CONTRAST
Clinical Indication: Right lower quadrant abdominal pain.
Technique: Standard protocol.
Findings: Dilated appendix measuring 11 mm with periappendiceal fat stranding. No abscess or free air.
Impression: Acute appendicitis without perforation.

documents.title: ED Provider Note
documents.text:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT NOTE
Chief Complaint: Left calf pain and swelling.
HPI: 46-year-old woman with left calf pain and swelling. Three days of left calf pain and swelling after a 9-hour flight. No chest pain or dyspnea.
ED Course: Left calf circumference 3 cm greater than right. Wells score 3.
Assessment:
1. Deep vein thrombosis, left popliteal vein
Disposition and Plan: Start rivaroxaban 15 mg BID for 21 days then 20 mg daily. Return precautions for chest pain or dyspnea.

documents.title: US Venous Duplex Left Lower Extremity
documents.text:
US VENOUS DUPLEX LEFT LOWER EXTREMITY
Clinical Indication: Left calf pain and swelling.
Technique: Standard protocol.
Findings: Non-compressible left popliteal and posterior tibial veins with occlusive echogenic thrombus.
Impression: Acute occlusive deep vein thrombosis of the left popliteal and posterior tibial veins.

documents.title: Discharge Summary
documents.text:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Chief Complaint: Fever and productive cough.
History of Present Illness: 75-year-old man presenting with fever and productive cough. Four days of fever to 39.2 C, productive cough with rust-colored sputum and pleuritic right-sided chest pain.
Hospital Course: Treated with ceftriaxone and azithromycin. Defervesced by hospital day 2. Oxygen weaned to room air.
Discharge Diagnoses:
1. Community-acquired pneumonia, right lower lobe
Discharge Plan: Complete 5-day course of oral amoxicillin-clavulanate. Repeat chest x-ray in 6 weeks.

documents.title: XR Chest PA and Lateral
documents.text:
XR CHEST PA AND LATERAL
Clinical Indication: Fever and productive cough.
Technique: Standard protocol.
Findings: Dense airspace opacity in the right lower lobe with air bronchograms. No pneumothorax.
Impression: Right lower lobe consolidation consistent with pneumonia.

encounter.reason: Shortness of breath and bilateral leg swelling

documents.title: Discharge Summary
documents.text:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Chief Complaint: Shortness of breath and bilateral leg swelling.
History of Present Illness: 67-year-old woman presenting with shortness of breath and bilateral leg swelling. Progressive exertional dyspnea over 10 days, 3-pillow orthopnea and a 4 kg weight gain. Reports running out of furosemide two weeks ago.
Hospital Course: Diuresed with IV furosemide with net negative 5.2 L. Transitioned to oral diuretic. Echocardiogram showed LVEF 30%.
Discharge Diagnoses:
1. Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
2. Essential hypertension
Discharge Plan: Furosemide 40 mg PO daily, daily weights, low-sodium diet, cardiology follow-up in 1 week.

documents.title: XR Chest 2 Views
documents.text:
XR CHEST 2 VIEWS
Clinical Indication: Shortness of breath and bilateral leg swelling.
Technique: Standard protocol.
Findings: Enlarged cardiac silhouette. Bilateral small pleural effusions. Pulmonary vascular congestion.
Impression: Cardiomegaly with pulmonary edema and bilateral pleural effusions.

documents.title: Office Visit Note
documents.text:
PROGRESS NOTE
Reason for Visit: Hypertension follow-up.
Subjective: 58-year-old man. Home blood pressures averaging 152/94. Adherent to amlodipine. No headache or chest pain.
Objective: Office blood pressure 156/96.
Assessment:
1. Essential hypertension
2. Hyperlipidemia
Plan: Add chlorthalidone 12.5 mg daily, repeat BMP in 2 weeks, continue home monitoring.

documents.title: ED Provider Note
documents.text:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT NOTE
Chief Complaint: Right flank pain.
HPI: 37-year-old man with right flank pain. Sudden severe colicky right flank pain radiating to the groin with nausea and gross hematuria.
ED Course: Pain controlled with ketorolac. Tolerating oral intake.
Assessment:
1. Right ureteral calculus with hydronephrosis
Disposition and Plan: Tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily, strain urine, urology follow-up within 1 week, return if fever.

documents.title: CT Abdomen and Pelvis without Contrast
documents.text:
CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITHOUT CONTRAST
Clinical Indication: Right flank pain.
Technique: Standard protocol.
Findings: 6 mm calculus at the right ureterovesical junction with mild right hydroureteronephrosis.
Impression: Obstructing 6 mm right UVJ calculus with mild hydronephrosis.

documents.title: ED Provider Note
documents.text:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT NOTE
Chief Complaint: Wheezing and chest tightness.
HPI: 24-year-old man with wheezing and chest tightness. Two days of wheezing after a viral illness. Using albuterol every 3 hours.
ED Course: Improved after three albuterol-ipratropium nebulizers and oral dexamethasone. Peak flow 78% predicted at discharge.
Assessment:
1. Moderate persistent asthma with acute exacerbation
Disposition and Plan: Start budesonide-formoterol, albuterol as needed, asthma action plan reviewed.

encounter.reason: Low back pain radiating to left leg

documents.title: Office Visit Note
documents.text:
PROGRESS NOTE
Reason for Visit: Low back pain radiating to left leg.
Subjective: 49-year-old man. Eight weeks of low back pain radiating down the posterior left leg to the foot. Failed 6 weeks of physical therapy.
Objective: Positive straight leg raise on the left. Strength 5/5. No bowel or bladder symptoms.
Assessment:
1. Lumbar disc herniation L4-L5 with left radiculopathy
Plan: Refer to spine clinic for epidural steroid injection evaluation, continue physical therapy.

documents.title: MRI Lumbar Spine without Contrast
documents.text:
MRI LUMBAR SPINE WITHOUT CONTRAST
Clinical Indication: Low back pain radiating to left leg.
Technique: Standard protocol.
Findings: Left paracentral disc extrusion at L4-L5 with left lateral recess stenosis contacting the descending L5 nerve root.
Impression: L4-L5 left paracentral disc extrusion with left lateral recess stenosis.

documents.title: Neurology Follow-up
documents.text:
PROGRESS NOTE
Reason for Visit: Post-TIA follow-up.
Subjective: No recurrent focal symptoms. Tolerating apixaban without bleeding.
Objective: Neurologic exam normal. Echocardiogram showed mildly dilated left atrium, LVEF 60%.
Assessment:
1. Transient ischemic attack, resolved
2. Atrial fibrillation on anticoagulation
Plan: Continue apixaban and atorvastatin. Recheck lipid panel in 3 months.

documents.title: Discharge Summary
documents.text:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Chief Complaint: Fever and confusion.
History of Present Illness: 85-year-old woman presenting with fever and confusion. Brought in by family for 1 day of confusion, fever to 38.9 C and dysuria.
Hospital Course: Blood and urine cultures grew E. coli. Treated with IV ceftriaxone and fluids. Mental status returned to baseline.
Discharge Diagnoses:
1. Sepsis due to urinary tract infection
2. Acute kidney injury
Discharge Plan: Oral cephalexin to complete 10 days, repeat BMP in 1 week, primary care follow-up.

documents.title: ED Provider Note
documents.text:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT NOTE
Chief Complaint: Sudden left arm weakness.
HPI: 64-year-old woman with sudden left arm weakness. Twenty minutes of left arm weakness and slurred speech that fully resolved before arrival.
ED Course: Neurologic exam normal on arrival. Telemetry showed atrial fibrillation with rates 90-110.
Assessment:
1. Transient ischemic attack
2. Atrial fibrillation, new onset
Disposition and Plan: Start apixaban 5 mg BID, atorvastatin 80 mg, outpatient echocardiogram and neurology follow-up.

documents.title: CT Head without Contrast
documents.text:
CT HEAD WITHOUT CONTRAST
Clinical Indication: Sudden left arm weakness.
Technique: Standard protocol.
Findings: No acute intracranial hemorrhage, mass effect, or territorial infarct. Mild chronic small vessel ischemic change.
Impression: No acute intracranial abnormality.

PROGRESS NOTE
Reason for Visit: Fatigue and lightheadedness.
Subjective: 39-year-old woman. Two months of fatigue, exertional lightheadedness and heavy menstrual bleeding.
Objective: Conjunctival pallor. Ferritin 6 ng/mL.
Assessment:
1. Iron deficiency anemia
Plan: Ferrous sulfate 325 mg every other day, gynecology referral, repeat CBC in 4 weeks.

documents.title: Office Visit Note
documents.text:
PROGRESS NOTE
Reason for Visit: Recurrent headaches.
Subjective: 33-year-old woman. Throbbing unilateral headaches 3-4 times per month with photophobia and nausea. No red-flag features.
Objective: Neurologic exam normal. MRI obtained given change in headache pattern.
Assessment:
1. Migraine without aura
Plan: Sumatriptan 50 mg as needed, headache diary, consider prophylaxis if frequency increases.

documents.title: MRI Brain without Contrast
documents.text:
MRI BRAIN WITHOUT CONTRAST
Clinical Indication: Recurrent headaches.
Technique: Standard protocol.
Findings: Normal brain parenchyma. No mass, hemorrhage or abnormal enhancement.
Impression: Normal MRI of the brain.
